items.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010
items.q: But I was always towards the Sonny thing. And then moving to New York, I was different. Because I was trying to play like Sonny

ctx.x: Not many people — well at least in my experience — have heard that played a lot.

Yeah, yeah, yeah. Yeah, because that’s my influence. I mean you know I remember when I was growing up, I mean like jazz growing up let’s put it that way, it was in the 70s and everybody started playing like Coltrane. And I like Coltrane, I mean he’s one of my influences too, and Joe Henderson and those guys. But I was always towards the Sonny thing. And then moving to New York, I was different. Because I was trying to play like Sonny and everybody else was going Trane, you know? I don’t know, it probably helped…
